name: ADS8688IDBTR
title: ADS8684 / ADS8688: 16-bit 500 kSPS SAR converters, 4 or 8 bipolar-capable channels, one 5 V supply
summary: Four-channel (ADS8684) and eight-channel (ADS8688) data acquisition chips: each channel has its own overvoltage clamp, programmable gain amplifier and antialiasing filter ahead of a multiplexer and one 16-bit SAR converter that runs at 500 kSPS shared over the scanned channels. From a single 5 V supply each channel takes ±10.24 V, ±5.12 V, ±2.56 V, 0 to 10.24 V or 0 to 5.12 V through a constant 1 MΩ, and survives ±20 V. A 4.096 V reference, an auxiliary direct input and an SPI-style port with daisy-chain input are built in; the digital side runs from 1.65 V to AVDD. TSSOP-38, -40°C to 125°C.
key_figures: AVDD 4.75 V to 5.25 V; DVDD 1.65 V to AVDD
13 mA typ (ADS8688), 8.5 mA typ (ADS8684) at 500 kSPS

circuits.title: Connections for the internal 4.096-V reference
circuits.description: REFSEL is tied to ground, so the internal reference is on and REFIO carries 4.096 V out. A 10 µF capacitor from REFIO to REFGND filters the reference noise; REFCAP, the buffered reference that feeds the ADC, has 1 µF and 22 µF to REFGND. REFGND and AGND go to ground; AVDD is the supply.

circuits.title: Connections for an external 4.096-V reference
circuits.description: REFSEL is tied to DVDD, which turns the internal reference off and makes REFIO an input. A REF5040 powered from AVDD drives REFIO, with CREF from its output to ground. The internal buffer still drives REFCAP, decoupled by 1 µF and 22 µF to REFGND; REFGND and AGND go to ground.
notes: U2.VIN is the REF5040 supply pin, marked AVDD at the REF5040; its other pins follow its own pinout.

circuits.title: Digital interface to a host controller
circuits.description: One converter on a host's serial port. The host drives CS, SCLK, RST/PD and its data output into SDI, and reads SDO on its data input. DAISY is tied to DGND because there is no device before it in a chain.

circuits.title: Daisy-chain connection
circuits.description: Several converters share the host's CS, SCLK and data-out lines, so all sample together and all take the same configuration word. Data ripple along the chain: the first device's DAISY is grounded, each SDO feeds the next device's DAISY, and the last SDO returns to the host. Reading N devices takes at least 16 × N SCLK edges after the 16-clock command field. The figure shows ADC1, ADC2 and the last, ADCN.
notes: Between ADC2 and ADCN the chain may hold more devices, each wired as ADC2.

circuits.title: Star connection
circuits.description: Several converters share SCLK and the host's data-out line, and their SDO pins join on the host's data input; each has its own CS line from the host. Only the selected device drives SDO, since SDO is high impedance while CS is high, so the host must hold just one CS low at a time.

circuits.title: 8-channel multiplexed data acquisition for power automation
circuits.description: Current and potential transformers deliver 50 Hz sine waves to the ADS8688 inputs, which run on a 5 V AVDD. Each channel has a balanced RC filter: one resistor into AIN_nP, a matching one into AIN_nGND from the grounded end of the transformer secondary, and a capacitor across the two pins. Channels 0 and 7 are shown; channels 1 to 6 repeat them. The conversion data go to a capture card and a PC that corrects the phase shift the multiplexer adds between channels.
notes: Input signal: single-ended sine of ±10 V amplitude at 50 Hz typical.

operation.text: Each input channel has its own overvoltage protection, programmable gain amplifier and second-order antialiasing filter, then a 4- or 8-way multiplexer feeds one 16-bit SAR ADC. The 500 kSPS throughput is shared across the channels scanned. A 4.096 V reference with a fast buffer and an SPI-style port with daisy-chain input are on chip. Everything runs from one 5 V analog supply, yet the inputs accept bipolar signals up to ±2.5 × VREF, so no high-voltage supplies or input drivers are needed.

Inputs are single-ended: AIN_nP carries the signal and AIN_nGND is the local ground sense, which may sit within ±0.1 V of GND. The converter measures AIN_nP - AIN_nGND. Each channel takes its own range: ±2.5, ±1.25 or ±0.625 × VREF, or 0 to 2.5 or 0 to 1.25 × VREF (±10.24 V, ±5.12 V, ±2.56 V, 0 to 10.24 V and 0 to 5.12 V with a 4.096 V reference). Where the sensor ground differs from the board ground, run a separate wire from AIN_nGND to the sensor or conditioning ground.

Every channel looks like a 1 MΩ resistance whatever the range, sample rate or signal frequency, so sources and sensors can usually connect directly. To hold dc accuracy, place a resistance on AIN_nGND equal to the source resistance on AIN_nP; this cancels the extra offset the source resistance adds.

Each input has internal protection: the 1 MΩ input resistors together with the PGA gain resistors (RFB, RDC) limit current, and anti-parallel diodes set the clamp. Powered, with AVDD at 5 V or below 30 kΩ to ground, inputs survive ±20 V; unpowered, with AVDD floating above 30 kΩ, ±11 V. Beyond these the internal transistors break down. Between the selected range and the protection limit the output saturates. The internal protection is a second line only; external parts against surge, ESD and EFT are recommended. A higher source impedance lowers the diode current and widens the protected range, but adds gain error and noise.

The PGA of each channel turns the single-ended input into a differential signal for the ADC and shifts its common mode. Its gain is set by Range_CHn[3:0]; the default, 0000, is ±2.5 × VREF. The resistor network and amplifiers are trimmed for low gain error on every channel and range.
A second-order low-pass filter after each PGA limits the front-end noise. Its -3 dB point is typically 15 kHz and its response is the same on every range.

An integrated driver in each channel settles the multiplexer output to 16 bits within the acquisition time when switching channels, whatever the levels on the channels. In manual mode (MAN_Ch_n) a register write picks the channel for each sample; with AUTO_RST scanning, the next channel is taken on every CS falling edge through the enabled channels in ascending order.

With REFSEL low or tied to AGND the 4.096 V internal reference is used and REFIO outputs it. Place at least 10 µF from REFIO to REFGND as close to REFIO as possible; with the band-gap's output impedance it forms a low-pass filter for the reference noise, and less capacitance means more noise and lower SNR and SINAD. REFIO can only source a little current: do not load it, except through a buffer amplifier such as the OPA320. Initial accuracy is trimmed to ±1 mV max; drift is 6 ppm/°C typ, 10 ppm/°C max.

Mechanical or thermal stress on the die shifts the reference; soldering and later reflows are the main cause. In a test of 80 parts through one lead-free reflow, all shifted positive, though negative shifts can occur, and each further reflow adds shift. On a board reflowed twice, solder the ADS868x in the second pass.

With REFSEL high or tied to DVDD the internal reference is off and a 4.096 V reference is applied at REFIO. The internal buffer still drives REFCAP, so a low-power or small external reference is suitable; filter its output to keep its noise down.

The buffer output on REFCAP drives the ADC reference. Put at least 10 µF from REFCAP to REFGND, plus 1 µF as close to REFCAP as possible for high frequencies. Do not load REFCAP. Its drift is 1 ppm/°C typ, 1.5 ppm/°C max.

AUX_IN and AUX_GND reach the ADC through the multiplexer with no protection, PGA or filter, so the only range is 0 V to VREF, with AUX_GND tied to GND. The input is sampled straight onto a 75 pF capacitor. A slow, low-impedance source can drive it directly; at higher throughput, signal frequency or source impedance use a driver amplifier with low output impedance (see the AUX driver equations). The AUX channel has 16-bit no-missing-codes performance.
Output codes are straight binary on every range and channel, bipolar and unipolar alike: NFS gives 0000h, mid-scale (FSR/2) 8000h and PFS - 1 LSB FFFFh.
Active low. The falling edge samples the channel chosen in the previous frame, starts the conversion on the internal clock and opens a frame. With CS high the ADC is idle.

All transfers are timed on SCLK falling edges. SDI is read on the first 16 falling edges of each frame; a new setting takes effect at the next CS falling edge. CS low releases SDO from high impedance; SDO stays low for 15 edges, puts out the MSB on the 16th edge and further bits on later edges, then goes low after the frame and high impedance when CS rises. The frame length depends on the SDO format setting.

RST/PD acts at any time, independent of the clock. A low pulse of 40 ns to 100 ns resets the program registers without powering down; 400 ns or longer enters power-down and resets the registers; 100 ns to 400 ns is not recommended. In power-down all digital inputs except RST/PD are ignored. After releasing RST/PD, write the program registers once and send AUTO_RST or MAN_Ch_n to begin converting.

A frame begins on the CS falling edge, which samples and starts conversion. The host clocks the next command into SDI over 16 SCLK edges while SDO stays low. The conversion finishes within those edges, so the 16th falling edge must come after tCONV; this caps SCLK. On the 16th edge the device takes the last SDI bit and outputs the MSB; a 16-bit result ends at edge 32, after which SDO outputs 0. CS high ends the frame and floats SDO.

No setting is needed for daisy-chain mode. All devices sample on the shared CS edge and take the same SDI word; at the end of conversion each loads its result into a 16-bit shift register, outputs its MSB on the 16th edge, and then on each edge shifts in DAISY and shifts out SDO. The host receives ADCN first, then ADCN-1 and so on. Throughput falls with the number of devices. Beyond four devices the shared CS, SCLK and data lines may be loaded enough to cause timing errors; buffer them.
A star frame is the same as a single device's. Keep to four devices at most on shared SDO and SCLK lines, or buffer them, to avoid timing errors from loading.

At power-up the device idles with default register values and waits for a command; configure it before converting. Holding SDI low (all 16 bits 0, NO_OP) keeps whichever of STDBY, PWR_DN, AUTO_RST and MAN_Ch_n was last chosen. A NO_OP during a program register access keeps the register settings and returns to IDLE.
CS must stay low until the 16th SCLK falling edge latches the command. If CS rises earlier the device goes to an INVALID state, returns invalid data on SDO and waits for a proper command.

Command 8200h enters STDBY on the next CS rising edge. Part of the circuit powers down but the reference and buffer stay on, and the registers keep their values. Registers can be written in 16 SCLK cycles and read normally; a 32-clock frame returns invalid data. To leave, write AUTO_RST or MAN_Ch_n; the exit begins on the next CS rising edge, and CS must stay high for at least 20 µs before the next falling edge so the circuits are biased before sampling.

PWR_DN switches off all circuits including the reference and buffer. Software power-down (command 8300h, entered on the next CS rising edge) keeps the register settings; hardware power-down through RST/PD resets them. Registers can be written and read in PWR_DN. To leave, write a valid command; the device exits on the next CS rising edge and, with the internal reference (REFSEL = 0), needs 15 ms before data are valid.

Command A000h scans the channels enabled in AUTO_SEQ_EN (01h) in ascending order, wrapping to the lowest after the highest; each channel uses its own range register. The command frame must be a full 32 SCLK cycles for the first channel of the next frame to be converted correctly. Sending A000h again restarts the sequence from the lowest enabled channel. Unselected channels can be powered down through register 02h.

A manual command (C000h to DC00h, or E000h for AUX) selects one channel; it is sampled at the next frame's CS falling edge and keeps being converted while SDI stays low. The command frame must be a full 32 SCLK cycles for the next channel to be converted correctly. A command takes effect on the next CS falling edge, so the data for a newly chosen channel arrive one frame later.

Command 8500h resets all program registers to default on the CS rising edge. The device stays in RST while SDI is low; registers can be written in 16 SCLK cycles and read normally; a 32-clock frame returns invalid data. Send AUTO_RST or MAN_Ch_n to begin converting with the default settings.

Command registers (16-bit, write-only) choose the mode: AUTO_RST or MAN_Ch_n, STDBY, PWR_DN, or RST. They read as all 0 after power-up or reset, and a command executes when CS rises at the end of its frame. Program registers set the AUTO_RST sequence, channel power-down, daisy-chain device ID, SDO format and each channel's range.

A program register access needs at least 24 SCLK cycles after CS falls. SDI bits 15-9 give the address and bit 8 the direction (1 write, 0 read). For a write, bits 7-0 are the data and SDO echoes them back over the next eight clocks for checking. For a read, bits 7-0 are don't care and SDO outputs the register's 8 bits MSB first from the 16th falling edge.

AVDD powers the internal circuits and DVDD the digital interface; each can be set anywhere in its range independently. Decouple each AVDD pin to AGND with at least 10 µF and 1 µF, the 1 µF nearest the pins, and place at least 10 µF very close to DVDD for the digital switching current. PSRR is better with the decoupling capacitors fitted.

Split the board into analog and digital areas and keep analog input and reference traces away from digital lines; use a single ground plane. AVDD: 1 µF X7R 0603, rated 10 V or more, close to the pins. DVDD: 10 µF X7R 0805, rated 10 V or more. No vias between the AVDD or DVDD pins and their capacitors; ground pins to the plane by short, low-impedance paths. REFCAP: 1 µF X7R 0603 near the pins plus 22 µF X7R 1210, both straight to the pins with no vias. REFIO: 10 µF ceramic close to the pins when the internal reference is used. Place the AUX RC filter parts close to the device; C0G (NP0) capacitors are the most stable over voltage, frequency and temperature.

An eight-channel module measuring ±10 V, ±5 V, ±2.5 V, 0 to 10 V and 0 to 5 V inputs (1 MΩ typical input impedance) and 0 to 20 mA, 4 to 20 mA and ±20 mA inputs (300 Ω), each channel set in software. The ADS8688 uses its own PGA and 4.096 V reference. An LM5017 fly-buck makes an isolated 6 V from 24 V, and an LDO gives the 5 V for the converter; an ISO7141CC isolates SPI and an ISO1541D isolates I2C to a TCA6408A that drives TLP3123 switches choosing voltage or current mode. Inputs have TVS and ESD diodes and an RC low-pass filter on each channel. Target accuracy is 0.2 % or better at 25°C.
